theme: Sharing; Ananias and Sapphira; the Seven appointed
readingInstruction: Read Acts 4:32-6:7. The church shares everything, Barnabas gives, Ananias and Sapphira lie to the Spirit, the apostles are arrested again, and seven men are chosen to serve. Notice the contrast between the true generosity and the false.
settingTheScene: The young church is growing rapidly under pressure from outside and now faces problems from inside. In these chapters, we see its generosity, the danger of hypocrisy, further persecution, and an organizational crisis over the care of widows. In each, the church responds in a way that preserves its witness.
observation: “Now the full number of those who believed were of one heart and soul, and no one said that any of the things that belonged to him was his own, but they had everything in common” (4:32).
“There was not a needy person among them” (4:34).
“Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and to keep back for yourself part of the proceeds of the land?” (5:3).
“And great fear came upon the whole church and upon all who heard of these things” (5:11).
“We must obey God rather than men” (5:29).
“Then they left the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer dishonor for the name” (5:41).
“Therefore, brothers, pick out from among you seven men of good repute, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we will appoint to this duty” (6:3).
“And the word of God continued to increase, and the number of the disciples multiplied greatly in Jerusalem” (6:7).
interpretation:
The church was of one heart and soul. The believers sold property and laid the proceeds at the apostles’ feet to be distributed to those in need. This was voluntary, not compulsory, and a spontaneous overflow of love. Barnabas, whose name means “son of encouragement,” sold a field and gave the money.

Ananias and Sapphira did the same, but they kept back part and pretended to give all. Peter says, “You have not lied to man but to God.” Both fall dead. The sin was not keeping part of the money. Peter says the land was theirs to keep. The sin was hypocrisy: pretending to be more generous than they were, to gain a reputation. Luke says great fear came on the whole church. God takes the purity of his church seriously.

The apostles continue to do signs, and the sick are brought into the streets. The high priest and the Sadducees are filled with jealousy and arrest them, but an angel opens the prison doors at night and tells them to go and preach. When they are brought before the council, they say: “We must obey God rather than men.” Peter again preaches Jesus, crucified and raised, to give repentance and forgiveness. The council wants to kill them, but Gamaliel, a respected teacher of the law, advises caution: if this is from men, it will fail; if it is from God, you cannot overthrow it. They flog the apostles and charge them not to speak in Jesus’ name. The apostles leave “rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer dishonor for the name.”

Then comes an internal problem. The Greek-speaking widows are being overlooked in the daily distribution. The apostles do not dismiss the complaint. They gather the disciples and propose that seven men be chosen to oversee this ministry, so that the apostles can devote themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word. The seven all have Greek names, suggesting they were from the complaining group. The church chooses them, the apostles pray and lay hands on them, “and the word of God continued to increase.” Stephen and Philip are among them. The church solves a problem by creating a ministry of service, a model for the later office of deacon.
connection: Deuteronomy 15:4 said there should be no poor among you if you obey. Joshua 7 is the story of Achan’s hidden sin, with a similar severity. Proverbs 21:3 says to do righteousness and justice. Matthew 6:1-4 warns against giving to be seen. Galatians 6:2 says to bear one another’s burdens. 1 Timothy 3:8-13 describes deacons. James 1:27 speaks of caring for widows. 2 Corinthians 9:7 says God loves a cheerful giver.
application:
Examine your own giving. Is it done for God or for a reputation? Give something in secret.

Pray for your church’s leaders, that they would devote themselves to prayer and the Word.

Where is someone being overlooked in your church? What could you do?
prayerPrompts: Thank God for the generosity of the early church.
Ask him to keep you from hypocrisy.
Ask him to teach you to give from a sincere heart.
